title: Lecture 2 Part 2 — Applications
description: Apply HTML table, form, control, and accessibility concepts to practical coding scenarios.
subject: Web Development

questions.question: You are building a table and need a cell to take up the space of three columns. Which attribute should you use?
questions.explanation: colspan="3" makes the table cell span three columns horizontally.

questions.question: If you want to group the bottom row of a table that contains the grand totals, which semantic element should you wrap around that row?
questions.explanation: <tfoot> semantically groups footer rows such as totals, apart from the table body.

questions.question: You have a `<th>` tag with the attribute `id="employeeName"`. To correctly associate a data cell with this header for screen readers, how should the `<td>` be coded?
questions.explanation: The value of headers references the id of the relevant <th>, explicitly associating this data cell with its header.

questions.question: You are creating a form to update a user profile. The form data includes sensitive information. Which method is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: POST sends form values in the request body instead of the URL. Use HTTPS as well when protecting sensitive data.

questions.question: A user clicks a button that clears all the fields they just typed into a form. What was the most likely code for that button?
questions.explanation: input type="reset" restores form controls to their initial values; it does not submit or delete server data.

questions.question: You want to ask users to select their favorite hobbies. They can choose multiple hobbies or none at all. Which input type is best?
questions.explanation: Checkboxes are independent, so users can select several hobbies or leave them all unchecked.

questions.question: You want to use a custom picture of a checkmark as the button users click to submit the form. Which code accomplishes this?
questions.explanation: input type="image" displays an image as a submit control; alt provides an accessible name for it.

questions.question: You are configuring an HTML5 email input field. Which code will automatically validate that the user entered something resembling an email address?
questions.explanation: input type="email" enables the browser’s basic email-format validation. It does not verify that the address exists.

questions.question: You want to add a slider control to your form that allows users to pick a number between 1 and 10. Which HTML5 input type should you use?
questions.explanation: input type="range" provides a slider. Set min="1" and max="10" to constrain its range.

questions.question: You need a multi-line box for users to leave a comment. You want it to be 5 rows tall and 40 characters wide. How do you code this?
questions.explanation: <textarea> supports multiple lines; rows controls visible height and cols controls visible width.

questions.question: You created a drop-down list of countries using `<select>`, but you want "Saudi Arabia" to be selected by default when the page loads. Which attribute do you add to its `<option>` tag?
questions.explanation: The selected attribute marks the option chosen initially when the dropdown is displayed.

questions.question: You are using a `<label>` element for a text box. The text box has the attribute `id="firstName"`. How should the label be coded to connect properly?
questions.explanation: The label’s for attribute must exactly match the input’s id to associate them.

questions.question: You want to group a customer's billing address fields together with a border and the title "Billing Info". Which two elements will you use?
questions.explanation: <fieldset> groups related controls and <legend> supplies the group’s caption.

questions.question: What happens when a user clicks an `<input type="submit">` button?
options: The browser executes a local JavaScript file exclusively.
The form data is packaged and sent to the server-side script specified in the form's `action` attribute.
The form is printed to the user's default printer.
questions.correctAnswer: The form data is packaged and sent to the server-side script specified in the form's `action` attribute.
questions.explanation: Submitting a form sends its controls’ values to the endpoint specified by the form’s action attribute.

questions.question: You want to provide a list of suggested colors (Red, Blue, Green) to a user in a text field, but you also want them to be able to type "Purple" if they want. Which element is best?
questions.explanation: <datalist> supplies suggestions to an input while still allowing values such as Purple that are not listed.

questions.question: If you want to prompt the user to use a calendar to pick a specific date for an appointment, which HTML5 input type is used?
questions.explanation: input type="date" represents a calendar date and commonly lets the browser show a date picker.

questions.question: You need to create a table cell that spans down across two rows vertically. Which code snippet is correct?
questions.explanation: rowspan="2" makes this cell extend vertically across two table rows.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common server-side scripting language that might process a form after submission?
questions.explanation: PHP is a server-side programming language that can receive and process submitted form data.

questions.question: You have a group of three radio buttons for "Credit Card Type" (Visa, MasterCard, Amex). To ensure only one can be clicked at a time, what must be true?
questions.explanation: Radio buttons with the same name are treated as one group, allowing only one selected value at a time.

questions.question: You want to add a text label directly inside a visual grouping box created by `<fieldset>`. Which tag do you place immediately after the opening `<fieldset>` tag?
questions.explanation: <legend> labels a fieldset and is placed as its first child to give the grouped controls a caption.
